items.text: $f$ flat: maximal points of $X$ go to maximal points of $Y$ (a generalization $y'$ of $y=f(x)$ lifts to a generalization $x'$ of $x$, $x'=x$).
For every closed irreducible $Y'\subset Y$ every component of $f^{-1}(Y')$ dominates a component of $Y'$; this characterizes generalizing morphisms. Example: $X_{k'}\to X$ for $k'/k$.
Examples of flatness
$Y$ regular of dimension one (Dedekind ring $A$): $M$ flat $\iff$ torsion-free.
A\ \text{domain},\ M\ \text{flat}\Rightarrow f\cdot\colon M\to M\ \text{injective for }f\neq0\qquad(\text{tensor }A\xrightarrow{f}A\text{ with }M)
Converse for a principal ideal domain: $M=\varinjlim M_i$ ($M_i$ of finite type, torsion-free, hence free); a filtering limit of flat modules is flat.
$X$ reduced over $Y$ of dimension one: $X$ flat over $Y$ $\iff$ every irreducible component of $X$ dominates (a component of) $Y$. In general: every associated cycle dominates.
$Y$ regular, $f$ of finite type, $X$ Cohen–Macaulay (e.g. regular): $f$ flat $\iff$ all fibres (all components of fibres) have the same dimension.
Flatness implies continuity of fibre dimension. Deeper: $Y$ normal, $f$ of finite presentation, universally open with separable fibres $\Rightarrow$ $f$ flat (EGA IV).
Faithfully flat: subschemes
$f\colon X\to Y$ faithfully flat. Then
\mathrm{SS}(Y)\longrightarrow\mathrm{SS}(X),\qquad Y'\longmapsto f^{-1}(Y')\ \ \text{is injective}
Proof: same underlying set ($f$ surjective); reduce to closed subschemes with quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal J',\mathcal J''\subset\mathcal O_Y$; $f^*$ is exact and faithful on modules.
Corollary
$S'\to S$ faithfully flat, $X,Y$ over $S$:
\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{S'}(X',Y')\ \ \text{injective}
Flat alone is not enough: for $s\notin\operatorname{im}(S'\to S)$, the fibres over $s$ become empty.
Proof: $Z=X\times_SY$; morphisms $X\to Y$ $\leftrightarrow$ subschemes of $Z$ projecting isomorphically onto $X$ (graphs), and $Z'\to Z$ is faithfully flat.
Next: which $h\colon X'\to Y'$ come from $X\to Y$ (compatible with descent data); then which $X'$ over $S'$ come from $S$.
Flat base change of direct images
$f\colon X\to Y$ coherent, $g\colon Y'\to Y$ flat, $X'=X\times_YY'$, $h\colon X'\to X$, $\mathcal F'=h^*\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent.
\begin{CD} X' @>{h}>> X\\ @V{f'}VV @VV{f}V\\ Y' @>{g}>> Y \end{CD}
g^*f_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow f'_*\mathcal F'\quad\text{(adjoint to }f'^*g^*f_*\mathcal F=h^*f^*f_*\mathcal F\to h^*\mathcal F=\mathcal F')
This canonical map exists for any commutative square of ringed spaces; it is an isomorphism when $f$ is coherent, $g$ flat and $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent; likewise
g^*R^if_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R^if'_*\mathcal F'
Affine case: cartesian square of rings $A,B,A',B'$, $M$ a $B$-module; direct image = restriction of scalars, inverse image = $\otimes$.
Recapitulation (lecture of 9 July)
$A\to B$ local homomorphism of local rings: flat $\iff$ faithfully flat $\iff$ $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ surjective.
Flat morphisms are universally generalizing; no vertical components. Faithfully flat $\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{SS}(Y)\to\mathrm{SS}(X)$ injective.
g^*f_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }f'_*\mathcal F'\quad\text{if }g\text{ flat, or if }f\text{ affine (then no flatness needed: }M\otimes_AA'=M\otimes_BB')
Flat descent of properties of morphisms
$S'\to S$ faithfully flat, $f\colon X\to Y$ over $S$, $f'$ its base change: if $f'$ has the property, so has $f$ (and conversely when the property is stable under base change). One may take $S=Y$.
$g$ surjective: $f$ surjective $\iff$ $f'$ surjective; $f$ radicial $\iff$ $f'$ radicial ($\Delta_{f'}$ is the base change of $\Delta_f$).
$g$ surjective and quasi-compact: $f$ quasi-compact (quasi-separated, coherent) $\iff$ $f'$ is.
Proof: reduce to $Y,Y'$ affine, so that $X,X'$ are quasi-compact spaces.
